transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… my wife wanted me to come in. She says I’m not eating enough. I don’t know, most days I just have coffee and toast in the morning, maybe some soup or vegetables later. Big meals just don’t seem necessary at my age.
Have you lost weight recently, or has your wife mentioned concerns about your weight?

She’s mentioned it, yes. My doctor said the number on the scale is… lower than it ought to be. I don’t really see the fuss. Being a bit lighter makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Do you worry about gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others say you're already underweight?
I suppose… yes, a bit. When my wife puts butter on things or gives me a full plate, I get uneasy. I just don’t want to start putting weight back on after keeping things under control.
Do you ever make yourself sick or use medications like laxatives or diet pills to control your weight?
No… I don’t do that sort of thing. I just try to keep meals small, that’s all.
Do you see yourself as overweight or notice specific parts of your body that you feel are too large, even if others don’t seem to notice it?

I wouldn’t say overweight exactly… but if my stomach looks a bit rounded in the mirror, I don’t like it. Makes me feel sort of sloppy. And if my belt’s a notch looser, well… I feel I’ve done something right.
Do you experience a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if it doesn't seem like a realistic concern to others?
Yes… I suppose I do. If my wife puts butter on something or gives me a full plate, I get nervous. I start thinking I’ll put weight back on and lose the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Has your concern about eating or your fear of gaining weight caused any problems with your daily activities, relationships, or work?

A little, I suppose. I still manage most things around the house. But my wife… she gets worried if I haven’t eaten much, so sometimes she cuts outings short, or tells me to sit out those community tours. I don’t like making a fuss about it.
How long have you felt this way about food and your weight?
I’m not really sure… it sort of crept up on me. Not something I marked on a calendar. Maybe it’s been a while, but I couldn’t say exactly.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical condition recently, such as cancer, gastrointestinal problems, or any illness that might affect your appetite or weight?
Not that I know of, no. I haven’t been told I’ve got anything like that recently.
Have you been diagnosed with a medical condition that has caused you to lose your appetite or avoid eating certain foods?
No… I don’t think so. Nobody’s told me I have some condition causing that.
Have you ever felt that your concerns about your body or weight were not just a matter of personal preference but something more serious or unusual that others don’t seem to understand?

I don’t know… I suppose I don’t see it that way. Folks my age don’t eat like they used to, and I’m still getting around, doing my chores and my tours. So I don’t really understand why everyone’s making such a fuss about my weight.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as thinner than you actually are, or do you feel like certain parts of your body are larger than they really are?

I don’t know about thinner exactly. I just… if my belt’s a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done something right. But if I catch my stomach looking a bit rounded in the mirror, even a little, I feel… sloppy, I suppose. Disappointed.
Do you find that your judgment about what and how much to eat is strongly influenced by how you perceive your body shape or weight?
I suppose it does, a bit. If my belt feels looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. But if I see my stomach looking even a little rounded, then… I don’t know, I feel sloppy. Disappointed.
Do your concerns about your weight or body shape cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your life in any way?

I wouldn’t say it stops me from doing things, exactly. I still manage most of my chores. But… my wife’s been fussing more lately, cutting outings short or telling me to sit out the community tours if she thinks I haven’t eaten enough. I don’t much like that.
Would you say that your weight or the way you look determines how you feel about yourself overall?
I suppose… more than I’d like to admit. If my belt’s a bit looser, I feel I’ve done right by myself. If my stomach looks even a little rounded, I feel… sloppy. Disappointed in myself.
